sources: "Disappointment Is the Lot of Women", address to the Woman's Rights Convention, Cincinnati, Ohio (October 1855)
evidence: https://onehistory.org/Speech-Stone.htm - the opening line of the 1855 Cincinnati convention speech text

author: Lucy Stone
quote: I wish that women, instead of being walking show-cases, instead of begging of their fathers and brothers the latest and gayest new bonnet, would ask of them their rights.
sources: "Disappointment Is the Lot of Women", address to the Woman's Rights Convention, Cincinnati, Ohio (October 1855)
evidence: https://onehistory.org/Speech-Stone.htm - 1855 Cincinnati convention speech text showing this sentence

author: Emmeline Pankhurst
quote: I do not come here as an advocate, because whatever position the suffrage movement may occupy in the United States of America, in England it has passed beyond the realm of advocacy and it has entered into the sphere of practical politics.
sources: "Freedom or Death", speech at Parsons Theater, Hartford, Connecticut (13 November 1913)
evidence: https://www.rev.com/transcripts/emmeline-pankhurst-freedom-or-death - transcript of the Hartford 'Freedom or Death' speech opening with this sentence
https://speakola.com/political/tag/PANKHURST - Speakola's text of the speech, excerpt beginning with this sentence
https://www.ctexplored.org/emmeline-pankhurst-freedom-or-death-in-the-fight-for-suffrage/ - names the occasion: Parsons Theater, Hartford, Connecticut, 13 November 1913

author: Sojourner Truth
quote: I have as much muscle as any man, and can do as much work as any man. I have plowed and reaped and husked and chopped and mowed, and can any man do more than that?
sources: Remarks at the Woman's Rights Convention, Akron, Ohio (29 May 1851), as reported by Marius Robinson in the Anti-Slavery Bugle (21 June 1851)
evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ain%27t_I_a_Woman%3F - Wikipedia article on the speech, quoting the Marius Robinson transcription published in the Anti-Slavery Bugle, 21 June 1851
https://teachingamericanhistory.org/library/document/remarks-at-the-women-rights-convention/ - document text of Truth's remarks at the 1851 convention

author: Sarah Grimke
quote: I ask no favors for my sex. I surrender not our claim to equality. All I ask of our brethren is, that they will take their feet from off our necks, and permit us to stand upright on that ground which God designed us to occupy.
sources: Letters on the Equality of the Sexes and the Condition of Woman (1838), Letter II, dated 17 July 1837
evidence: https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/culture-magazines/letters-equality-sexes - encyclopedia entry on the Letters giving this passage and placing it in Letter 2, dated July 17, 1837
https://teachingamericanhistory.org/document/letters-on-the-equality-of-the-sexes-and-the-condition-of-women/ - document text of the Letters
https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Sarah_Grimk%C3%A9 - Wikiquote page for Sarah Grimke returned for this fragment

author: Anna Julia Cooper
quote: Only the BLACK WOMAN can say 'when and where I enter, in the quiet, undisputed dignity of my womanhood, without violence and without suing or special patronage, then and there the whole Negro race enters with me.'
sources: A Voice from the South (1892)
evidence: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anna-julia-cooper/a-voice-from-the-south/text/single-page - full text of A Voice from the South (1892) returned for this exact sentence
https://teachingamericanhistory.org/document/a-voice-from-the-south/ - document page for A Voice from the South, Aldine, Xenia, Ohio, 1892

author: Lucretia Mott
quote: she asks nothing as favor, but as right, she wants to be acknowledged a moral, responsible being
sources: "Discourse on Woman", address at the Assembly Buildings, Philadelphia (17 December 1849)
evidence: https://openbooks.library.umass.edu/giftsofspeech/chapter/lucretia-mott-discourse-on-woman-december-17-1849/ - text of the Discourse on Woman, dated December 17, 1849, containing this clause

author: Carrie Chapman Catt
quote: When a just cause reaches its flood-tide … whatever stands in the way must fall before its overwhelming power.
sources: "Is Woman Suffrage Progressing?", presidential address to the Sixth Convention of the International Woman Suffrage Alliance, Stockholm (13 June 1911)
evidence: https://wist.info/catt-carrie-chapman/43298/ - WIST entry giving this wording cited to the Stockholm address 'Is Woman Suffrage Progressing?' (13 June 1911)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_Conference_of_the_International_Woman_Suffrage_Alliance - confirms Catt's presidential address at the Stockholm conference, 13 June 1911

author: Angelina Grimke
quote: Human beings have rights, because they are moral beings
sources: Letters to Catherine E. Beecher, in Reply to an Essay on Slavery and Abolitionism (1838)
evidence: https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/literature-and-writing/analysis-sphere-woman-and-man-moral-beings-same - research-starter analysis of Grimke's letter on the sphere of woman and man as moral beings, quoting this line from Letters to Catherine E. Beecher (1838)

author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
quote: When the mother of the race is free, we shall have a better world.
sources: Women and Economics (1898)
evidence: https://open.oregonstate.education/sociologicaltheory/chapter/gilman-on-women-and-economics-1898/ - open textbook reproducing excerpts of Women and Economics (1898); result gives this as the closing statement of the work

author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
quote: What we do modifies us more than what is done to us. The freedom of expression has been more restricted in women than the freedom of impression, if that be possible.
sources: Women and Economics (1898)
evidence: https://open.oregonstate.education/sociologicaltheory/chapter/gilman-on-women-and-economics-1898/ - open textbook reproducing Women and Economics (1898) excerpts, showing this passage

author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
quote: We see the human mother worked far harder than a mare, laboring her life long in the service, not of her children only, but of men; husbands, brothers, fathers, whatever male relatives she has
sources: Women and Economics (1898)
evidence: https://open.oregonstate.education/sociologicaltheory/chapter/gilman-on-women-and-economics-1898/ - open textbook reproducing Women and Economics (1898), showing this passage on women's unpaid labour

author: Margaret Sanger
quote: The most far-reaching social development of modern times is the revolt of woman against sex servitude. The most important force in the remaking of the world is a free motherhood.
sources: Woman and the New Race (1920), Chapter 1, "Woman's Error and Her Debt"
evidence: https://content.csbs.utah.edu/~dlevin/AmPolTho/Sanger-Woman-and-the-New-Race.pdf - full text of Woman and the New Race (1920); opening of Chapter 1 'Woman's Error and Her Debt' gives this wording

author: Ida B. Wells
